title: review: P6b: complementary reviewer roles for two-review tasks behind [review].complementary = false — the first review gets role acceptance (criteria, functional correctness, regressions, tests), the second role adversarial (adversarial reasoning, security, edge cases, hidden assumptions); the review packet gains a role section; the security checklist section is unchanged and fires for both roles whenever its conditions hold; disabled means today's prompts byte for byte
spec:
Phase I P6 (brief inlined: for tasks requiring two reviewers avoid paying twice for nearly identical analysis; investigate role specialisation, A: acceptance criteria, functional correctness, regressions, tests; B: adversarial reasoning, security, edge cases, hidden assumptions; security-path requirements remain deterministic; current policy is the floor). Base goal/T-0489 after P6a1 (T-0491) merges (constraints.reviewer_role is read by attribution.review_facts). Work only in your own worktree and commit only on your own branch. Scout facts (T-0490): daemon._open_reviews (daemon.py:831-868) creates n_reviews review tasks, the second non-security review on the other tier (_other_tier) or review_tier for Claude-executed tasks, security reviews with complexity max(c, 7) and _security_review_tier; reviews_expected (daemon.py:706-717) is 2 from [review].two_reviews_from (default 7); review_packet (spawn.py:412-471) has spec, acceptance, scope, diff, changed tests, gate, security (conditions listed in the code), fix-round context; .orchestrator/prompts/review.md is {{packet}} plus fixed instructions; the adversarial-review skill returns verdict and comments only.
1. pool.toml [review] complementary = false (comment: when true, two-review tasks get role-specialised packets; default false keeps one prompt for both reviewers; measured with scorecard --reviews --by role before any default change).
2. daemon._open_reviews: when [review].complementary is true and n_reviews == 2, the first created review gets constraints.reviewer_role = "acceptance" and the second "adversarial"; a security review keeps its tier, complexity bump and review_reason exactly as today and additionally gets reviewer_role "adversarial" when it is the second review, "acceptance" when it is the first; single-review tasks get no role (attribution reports "general"); when complementary is false, nothing about review creation changes (assert byte-identical task dicts in a test).
3. spawn.review_packet(task, reviewed): when the review task has constraints.reviewer_role, append a "## role" section after gate and before security: acceptance -> "Focus: every acceptance criterion met by the diff, functional correctness, regressions in touched code paths, tests present and meaningful for each acceptance id; leave security and adversarial edge cases to the second reviewer unless blocking"; adversarial -> "Focus: adversarial reasoning about the diff, security and privilege boundaries, edge cases and failure modes, hidden assumptions and untested paths; leave acceptance bookkeeping to the first reviewer unless blocking". The security section keeps its existing conditions and content for both roles. Without a role the packet is unchanged (existing P1b tests stay green byte for byte).
4. Run rows: reviewer_role already flows through P6a1; make sure review_packet's header sources name the role so packet_version differs between the two roles.
Tests tests/test_daemon.py: test_open_reviews_assigns_acceptance_and_adversarial_roles_when_complementary, test_open_reviews_unchanged_when_complementary_false (task dicts identical to the pre-change behaviour), test_open_reviews_security_review_keeps_tier_bump_and_gets_role; tests/test_spawn.py: test_review_packet_role_section_for_each_role, test_review_packet_security_section_present_for_both_roles_on_security_path, test_review_packet_without_role_unchanged. Existing tests green; full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exit 0; commit with the task id including every named test; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: [review].complementary defaults to false and leaves review creation and packets unchanged; when true two-review tasks get acceptance and adversarial roles and the security section still fires on its own conditions
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree; the commit is on this task's own branch
